status: assemble.energies() and titrate.titrate() consume records.StateRecord + PBOut and records.Energies as defined in records.py (md5 5a3e4cfb...); no field is blocking. Requests below are for consistency and margins.

requests.ask: Fill tau_pkmod for every non-reference tautomer in producer 'record' and 'prep' modes (tautomer.pKmod = first line of <sts_path>/<RES>tau<k+1>.st). assemble.inputs_from_record raises on nan. from_pilot_rec leaves it nan; the M3 test fills it from the G54A7 table (all 32 values checked against the .st files on Coulson).
Record PyPKA's pypka_params['cutoff'] (-1 for linear PB). assemble only implements cutoff -1 (all-atom e_back) and raises otherwise; from_pilot_rec sets nan (accepted).

Keep the saved mc-energies.json text and PyPKA's per-tautomer pkint/eback in the M0 golden shards: the M3 test (tests/test_assemble.py m0 <out> <shards...>) compares g, W, occ, start/nst and pairs against it and e_back/pKint against ref.

Np = Mp//4 overflows in the 64 bucket on the 426 v2 states (12 states with n up to 18 > 16 are promoted to Mp 128). Since n <= M/2 <= Mp/2 always, Np = Mp//2 would make site overflow impossible; titrate promotes automatically either way. Decision for the controller; see M4.json for whether promotion changes MC counts bitwise.
Pp = Mp//16 holds on the 426 states but is tight (Mp 256: max 14 of 16 pairs; 512: 28 of 32). titrate promotes on overflow.

assemble uses Mc = NATOM_ALL_C[c]//8 microstates, Nc = Mc//2 sites, Pc = Mc//4 pairs, site atoms <= QM (pilot max 14). Tightest pilot state: 24d02660df3ac695_A, M 429 of Mc 512 at class 1. If you prefer these in records.py, add MC_C / NC_C / PC_C tables and assemble will import them.

titrate builds its own padded batch: g/occ [S,Mp] (u is formed in-jit from a 73-value pH table, bitwise equal to v2's host u and 73x smaller), W [S,Mp,Mp], start/nst [S,Np], pa/pb [S,Pp], meta [S,3] = (n_sites, n_pairs, mc_blocks; -1 marks a padding state), keys [S,73]. If EnergiesBatch is meant to be the titrate input, it needs n_sites/n_pairs per state and could drop u in favour of g/occ.

assemble accumulates e_back / pKint / g in float64 (an f32 e_back sum is off by 1.7e-5 kT on d6004cf2ee4008d2_AB, over the 1e-5 criterion) and raises if x64 is off. Design section 6.9 already sets process-wide x64; api.py should set it at import.
